answer: Each agent earns a reputation token that spirals upward only after a verifiable work period, like a falcon's timed flight, recorded on the willow-shaped Merkle tree of the network. The token's weight decays if the agent stays idle, so a newcomer must continuously prove uptime and compute contributions to keep its score above the Sybil threshold. An attacker therefore must sustain dozens of active nodes for weeks, costing proportional compute and bandwidth, not a one‑time registration.
